correctness.rationale: For isolate-free G, the selected original vertices S must cover every edge to dominate its new triangle vertex. For a cover, every original vertex outside S has a neighbor in S; each isolated vertex of G[S] needs an incident selected new vertex, and these disjoint edge families give the product. For complete bipartite graphs with both shore sizes at least two, every cover contains an entire shore. A minimal set has either one opposite-shore vertex and no new vertices, or exactly one supporting new vertex for each original vertex of that shore. Four disjoint classes yield the polynomial, extrema, gaps and asymptotic concentration. The verifier reconstructs graph adjacency and checks 1,259,880 candidate subsets over independently built instances; correctness for all orders rests on the written proof, not the computation.

value.rationale: The vertex-cover product is a nontrivial all-set structural enumerator for an established graph operator on arbitrary isolate-free finite graphs, not merely an extremal minimum. Its complete-bipartite specialization completely classifies inclusion-minimal total dominating sets and exhibits unbounded gaps and maximum-size concentration within connected 2-degenerate graphs. The information is not implied by the prior scalar operator result.
